newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian state workers to stage new strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian state workers to stage new strike.

text.p: Colombia's public sector workers will stage another strike before the end of the month to press demands for the fulfillment of accords that ended a nationwide work stoppage in February, a top union official said Friday.
Wilson Borja, head of the state workers' union known as Fenaltrase, said the strike would take place sometime during the week beginning June 23 and may last indefinitely.
"It all depends on the conditions that we see between now and then," Borja told Reuters when asked about the duration of the strike, which would be the second this month.
Colombia's estimated 800,000 state workers joined in a one- day strike Wednesday to demonstrate support for striking public health workers, who have been manning picket lines since June 3.

In addition to solidarity with health workers, Borja said the new strike would be held to protest against the government's neo- liberal economic policies and privatization program, which he said had been dictated to the government by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
"They've given orders to the government and it has to carry them out," Borja said.

The government agreed, as part of its accord with fiercely nationalistic union leaders in February, to analyze its privatization plans on a case-by-case basis and delay the opening of some sectors of the economy to private competition.

"We're against privatizations and we've always been against neo-liberal policies," Borja said, citing recent moves to end the state-run telecommunications company's monopoly over long distance telephone service as one alleged violation of the February accords.

Borja said Fenaltrase also strongly opposed the government's continuing selloff of power generation assets, since it had led to sharp cuts in subsidies and a dramatic increase in electricity rates over the last year.
